To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the readiness potential, which is the slow cortical potential associated with the preparation for voluntary movements, is a cortical phenomenon, and that it has a bilateral distribution over the precentral region of the brain.

the readiness potential is a cortical potential that is maximal over the precentral region of the scalp and is larger over frontal areas than over occipital areas, that the readiness potential increases with the intensity of the voluntary movement, that the readiness potentials are not correlated with the phase of the EEG alpha rhythm, that the readiness is followed by a complex cortical potential with an early bilateral positivity that begins 30 to 90 msec after the movement onset, and that the late potentials after voluntary and passive movements are similar
the brain potentials preceding voluntary movements, called the readiness potential, have a slow negative component, and that passive movements are accompanied by a complex surface-positive potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the brain controls the body.
the analysis of brain potentials accompanying voluntary movements.
the problem of the relation of brain potentials to the central nervous processes preceding voluntary movements and to the central nervous activity accompanying passive movements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the readiness potential and the potentials after voluntary and passive movement are related to each other, and that all of these are components of the cerebral evoked potential.
the readiness potential and the reafferent potentials are two distinct and separate components of the brain potentials preceding and following voluntary movement.
this method of analysis has provided a basis for further research into cerebral potentials and their relationship to behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the readiness potential represents the activity of a cortical mechanism which prepares the subject for a voluntary movement and is probably identical with a mechanism that is involved in the execution of voluntary movements.
the readiness potential is a cortical potential that is generated during voluntary movement preparation.
the readiness potential is a pre-motor phenomenon, which is related to the intention to act, and not to the actual movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a very complex organ that has many functions that are not fully understood.
the human brain has the ability to predict and plan movements.
the readiness potential can be recorded from different points on the scalp.
